name: Leon Black

summary.text: Leon Black is a co-founder of Apollo Global Management. In January 2021 Apollo published the results of a review by the law firm Dechert which found that Black had paid Jeffrey Epstein $158 million between 2012 and 2017 for tax and estate planning advice, found no evidence that Black was involved in Epstein's crimes, and noted the fees far exceeded what Black paid other advisers; Black announced he would step down as CEO. The Senate Finance Committee opened an inquiry into the arrangements in 2023, stating that the trusts and structures aimed to avoid over $1 billion in future gift and estate taxes. In January 2023 Black agreed to pay the U.S. Virgin Islands $62.5 million for a release from Epstein-related claims, without admitting liability. Separate civil suits against him alleging sexual misconduct have been dismissed, dropped or remain allegations; Black denies wrongdoing.

facts.claim: Apollo's review by Dechert LLP, released January 25, 2021, found that Black paid Epstein $158 million for advice on tax and estate planning and related services between 2012 and 2017, loaned him over $30 million and donated $10 million to his charity. Apollo said the review found no evidence Black was involved in Epstein's criminal activities.
facts.quote: Apollo said the Dechert investigation found "no evidence that Mr. Black was involved in any way with Mr. Epstein's criminal activities at any time."

facts.claim: On January 25, 2021 Apollo announced Black would step down as CEO no later than July 31, 2021, with co-founder Marc Rowan succeeding him, and that it would eliminate the special voting shares giving the co-founders effective control; Black said he deeply regretted his involvement with Epstein.

facts.claim: On July 25, 2023 Senate Finance Committee Chairman Ron Wyden announced an ongoing investigation into Black's tax planning and financial ties with Epstein, stating that it had uncovered serious tax issues with trusts and structures Black executed to avoid over $1 billion in future gift and estate taxes; the committee's letter cited the Dechert report's statement that a step-up-basis transaction could save Black another $600 million.

facts.claim: Black's racketeering suit against Guzel Ganieva, her lawyers at Wigdor LLP, Josh Harris and Steven Rubenstein was dismissed with prejudice by a federal judge in Manhattan on June 30, 2022, who called the claims 'glaringly deficient'; a federal appeals court later unanimously upheld the dismissal. Ganieva's own defamation suit against Black was dismissed in May 2023 on the basis of a 2015 nondisclosure agreement, a ruling a state appeals court upheld 4-1. Her allegations against Black were never adjudicated; Black denies them.
facts.quote: Black's racketeering suit was thrown out by a federal judge in Manhattan, who called the claims "glaringly deficient in fundamental respects" in dismissing them with prejudice

facts.claim: A July 2023 suit by a Jane Doe in the Southern District of New York (No. 23-cv-06418) alleged that Black sexually assaulted her at Epstein's Manhattan residence in 2002; Black's lawyer called it frivolous and sanctionable. The judge later sanctioned the plaintiff and her former counsel for misconduct but allowed the case to proceed. A separate suit by Cheri Pierson was dropped in February 2024. These are allegations only.
facts.quote: Judge Jessica Clarke sanctioned both Doe and her former lawyer, Jeanne Christensen of the Wigdor firm, citing serious misconduct, including that Christensen had repeatedly lied to the court and that Doe had falsified certain sonogram images. Despite these sanctions, Clarke ruled that the underlying lawsuit against Black could proceed.

openQuestions: The '$1 billion in tax savings' is the Senate Finance Committee's characterization of the intended effect of the trust structures, not an IRS or court determination. The gap between $158 million (Dechert, 2024-25 letters) and $170 million (2026 letters/report) is not explained in the sources.
The 2026 Senate materials are from the committee's ranking member (minority), so recorded as 'documented' rather than 'court' except for the 2023 chairman's inquiry findings.
Apollo's own January 2021 press release text was not retrieved; findings are cited via CNBC/Forbes/NBC coverage of the Dechert report.

The site's claim that Black paid '$158M for tax structures' matches the Dechert figure; the site's framing of Apollo as having 'gained' is not supported: the shareholder suit alleges Epstein never invested in Apollo funds and Apollo never retained him.
Jane Doe v. Black current status not confirmed beyond the sanctions ruling; the Ganieva and Pierson matters ended without adjudication of the underlying allegations.
